prompt: Our company gives a 20% discount to users whose 'engagement score' falls below 50 (it's an internal metric we compute). I want to know if the discount actually drives those users to come back. What's the cleanest way to estimate this?
assertions: Claude recommends regression discontinuity design (RDD) or describes the comparison of units just above vs. just below the cutoff
Claude mentions at least one key RDD assumption (no manipulation/gaming of the running variable, smoothness/continuity through the cutoff, or similar)
Claude notes that the estimate is local to the cutoff and may not generalize to users far from the threshold
Claude does NOT default to 'just regress retention on discount with controls' without mentioning the discontinuity structure
